units.translation: know that you have already stirred up a new war
so that either young children and widowed women lament to one another to return home
truly it is divine, not false
if there is anything divine, not false
and upon the children he invoked curses – and that they should one day obtain by iron-wielding hand
or for, or even, or then
I was, imperfect of the verb εἰμί, which see
to be young, to be vigorous
I am young, I am vigorous
Tyrwhitt rightly [reads] ὥστ᾽ ἀνηβησαί με γηραιᾷ φρενί [so that I might grow young again in my aged mind], i.e. to become young again.

in Plutarch, Moralia 454e (φλόξ συνεῖλεν [the flame seized]) ὑψηλὸν ἠβάσασα τεκτόνων πόνον [having made vigorous the lofty toil of the builders], where Heathius [reads] ἡβήσασα [having made vigorous], more aptly ἀμφιβᾶσα [having encompassed] Paleius.
old in mind, but flourishing in flesh
for the old always flourish in learning well
and indeed there is need of one who is vigorous
so that I might grow young again in my aged mind
the city will not blame an old messenger, but one vigorous in eloquent mind
so that I might grow young again in my aged mind
the flame seized, having made vigorous the lofty toil of the builders
Not rarely the young people themselves are called ἥβη [youth].
the one still lacking in the prime of youth
for old age is more just than youth
so that the city of the Persians groans, longing for the dearest youth of the land
what youth of allies he destroyed
and the land laments its native youth
leaders of the youth of Hellas, of one mind
not having granted the youth to possess fully beyond fate
let the flower of youth be unplucked
to lead the way, to lead, to hold command, to consider
of whom power wishes to lead
the right wing first, in good order, led the way in formation
but you lead, city-protecting sons of Cranaus, these resident aliens
to an unexpected house, as Justice may lead
for I prophesy, as the god may lead
we shall yield to these leaders who disgrace the house
and never consider self-will better than good counsel
consider all enemies of the gods more
for even living you considered him greater than your father
leader of thirty thousand black horse
Earth and other leaders of the underworld
for Medus was the first leader of the army
the old leader of the Achaean ships
and she herself, the leader, having furled the sail under the earth, rows with all oars
Μαγνητικὴν δὲ γαῖαν ἔς τε Μακεδόνων χώραν ἀφικόμεσθα [we came to the Magnesian land and to the country of the Macedonians], where Robortellus [reads] ἠδὲ [and] for ἔς τε [and to].
Thus I corrected for διὰ δ᾽ Ἰαόνων χέρας [and through the hands of the Ionians].
Thus Turnebus for εἰς δέ [and into].
Amistres and Artaphrenes and Megabates and Astaspes
they founded them bereft of men and unmanned
and the hands of the Ionians
and they directed all the walled mints
and Rhodes and Cnidus and the Cyprian cities, Paphos and Soli
